description: The Fire Monkey in Chinese astrology: personality, Fire element traits, 1956 and 2016 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Fire Monkey is the Monkey born in a Fire year, one of five versions of the ninth animal. It combines the Monkey's ingenuity with Fire's qualities. Fire Monkey years between 1924 and 2044 are 1956 and 2016. The Monkey's fixed element is Metal.

sections.heading: The Fire Monkey personality
paragraphs: Fire controls Metal, and the Monkey's fixed element is Metal, so a Fire stem is said to heat and challenge this nimble animal, turning cleverness into bold, competitive energy. Fire Monkeys are frequently cast as dynamic, adventurous and ambitious, with sparkling humour and plenty of nerve. They usually enjoy a challenge, love to win and can be dazzlingly persuasive when they want something. Their confidence attracts followers and their curiosity keeps them experimenting. The pressure of Fire on Metal also generates friction. Impatience, a competitive streak that can tip into rivalry, and a tendency to bend rules when they seem inconvenient are traits that turn up in traditional descriptions of this combination.

Belonging to the south and to the height of summer, Fire brings brightness, drive and visibility to any sign it colours. Classical texts connect it with enthusiasm, leadership and the urge to be seen and to make an impression. A Fire stem tends to make an animal more expressive, more daring and more openly emotional than its usual reputation suggests. People born in Fire years are often described as inspiring company and natural motivators. The caution most readings attach is a short fuse and a difficulty with slow seasons, when steady effort matters more than spark and the reward is a long way off.

sections.heading: Fire Monkey at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Fire is usually linked with initiative, persuasion and visible leadership. Fire-year people are often described as the ones who launch things, pitch ideas and keep morale high when a deadline looms, which suits performance, sales, media, entrepreneurship and campaigning of every kind. They tend to thrive on momentum and recognition. The traditional caution concerns stamina and follow-through: a Fire stem may lose patience with routine detail, so pairing with methodical colleagues and pacing energy across a project usually helps.

Bold, clever and competitive, the Fire Monkey enjoys being the sharpest strategist in the building. Entrepreneurship, trading, comedy, marketing and technology leadership are frequent associations, since quick thinking and showmanship win attention there. It needs a challenge big enough to hold its interest and the freedom to improvise when the plan stalls. Routine admin, left unchecked, tends to pile up on its desk. In love, the Fire Monkey is exciting, flirtatious and generous, keen on surprise trips and elaborate jokes. It needs stimulation and admiration. The familiar friction is a competitive streak that follows it home: it may treat arguments like a game to win, and a partner can feel outmanoeuvred rather than understood.

sections.heading: Fire Monkey years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Fire Monkey years are 1956 (February 12, 1956 to January 30, 1957) and 2016 (February 8, 2016 to January 27, 2017). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1956 anyone born before Feb 12 is a Wood Goat, not a Fire Monkey. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Fire Monkey year is Yang, matching the Monkey's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Bing-Shen, joining the heavenly stem Bing to the earthly branch Shen. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Goat year (before February 12, 1956) and the Wood Goat year (before February 8, 2016), and births in the weeks after each Fire Monkey year ends belong to the Fire Rooster. The new year itself fell on a Sunday in 1956 and Monday in 2016.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Fire Monkey
paragraphs: Fire Monkeys tend to benefit from directing their competitiveness at the problem rather than the people around them. Framing work as a challenge to solve together keeps relationships intact. Because they enjoy risk, building a few safety margins into plans, money set aside, a second opinion, protects their ventures. They may also need to practise patience with detail and follow-through. Honest feedback from friends who are not dazzled by their charm is valuable. Vigorous activity helps burn off restlessness. When ambition is tempered by integrity, Fire Monkeys become inspiring, inventive leaders.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Fire Monkey shares the Monkey's San He trine with the Rat and Dragon (the Water trine), its Liu He bond with the Snake, and its Liu Chong clash with the Tiger. The element adds a second layer: another Fire sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Fire in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Fire Monkey years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1956 (from February 12, 1956) and 2016 (from February 8, 2016). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Fire Monkey's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Fire and the Monkey's fixed element is Metal; in the five-element cycles fire controls Metal. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Fire Monkey?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rat and Dragon (San He) and the Snake (Liu He). The Tiger is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Fire Monkey called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Bing-Shen. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Fire stem Bing, followed by its earthly branch, here Shen for the Monkey, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Fire Monkey different from other Monkeys?
faq.answer: All Monkeys share ingenuity, humour and curiosity. The Fire year element changes the tone: fire is the element of summer and full daylight, and a Fire year is traditionally said to turn up the volume of whatever animal it meets.
